RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, February 23, 2010/Phalguna 4, 1931 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Civil Aviation; Finance; Health and Family Welfare; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Panchayati Raj; Petroleum
and Natural Gas; Rural Development; Shipping)
Total number of questions — 20
1
Complaints against oil marketing
companies
*1. SHRI MOHAMMED ADEEB:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the details of complaints received
against Indian Oil, Hindustan Petroleum,
Bharat Petroleum, Indane Gas, HP Gas and
Bharat Gas during the last and the current
financial years, so far;
(b) the details of action taken in each of
these cases;
(c) whether it is a fact that inspite of
these complaints malpractices and
irregularities are continuing unabated in
these companies; and
(d) if so, the steps being taken to prevent
recurrence thereof?
Violation of FEMA in Goa
*2. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN
NAIK: Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of
violations of Foreign Exchange Management
Act (FEMA) in the State of Goa;
(b) if so, the number of prosecutions
made and Show Cause Notices issued in
the last three years;
(c) the action taken against persons
violating the law in the last three years; and
(d) the nature of offences or violations
committed in the last three years?
World Bank loan for watershed
project in J and K
*3. SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL
DARDA: Will the Minister of FINANCE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that World Bank
has put up a disclaimer clause in return for
a Rs. 740 crore loan it has sanctioned for a
Watershed Project in Jammu and Kashmir;
(b) if so, whether this has been done by
the World Bank because of their wrong
perception that Jammu and Kashmir being

2
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
a “disputed territory”, this loan sanction
may not be used as a “certificate” for Jammu
and Kashmir being an integral part of India;
and
(c) whether the matter has been sorted
out and the loan amount has been
disbursed, as has been the practice in respect
of earlier World Bank funded projects in
Jammu and Kashmir in 1991 and 1999?
Poor air services in North-Eastern
Region
*4. SHRI KUMAR DEEPAK DAS:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIA TION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has worked
out any plan to overcome the poor air
services in the North-Eastern Region and
blatant flouting of the Route Dispersal
Guidelines (RDG) by the private
operators;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) what are the reasons for services
provided by the State carrier Indian Airlines
being below the average performance of the
regional air service, operating in the North-
Eastern Region; and
(d) whether the Civil Aviation Authority
is taking any corrective steps for providing
better quality services to the North-Eastern
Region, giving priority to better ground
transport facilities?
Market pricing of petroleum products
*5. SHRI PENUMALLI MADHU:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ministries
of Power and Chemicals and Fertilizers are
opposing his Ministry’s move to hike
administered price of gas with a shift to
market pricing after three years;
(b) whether any assessment has been
made about the adverse impact of this on
input costs of the existing gas-based Power
and Fertilizer plants; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
New facility of booking LPG cylinders
†*6. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the
Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is going to provide the facility of booking
cooking gas cylinders to consumers in Delhi
only by Short Messaging System (SMS)
and Interactive V oice Response System
(IVRS);
(b) whether Government has conducted
any inquiry regarding the extent to which
people are satisfied with this system in the
areas where it is already in force;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps being taken by
Government to fix the responsibility of
distributors and to provide gas to
consumers on time?
Disbursal of agriculture loan
†*7.  SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
nationalized banks, along with private
banks, have remained behind in achieving
the loan target for the agriculture sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether any such policy has been
formed for future so that all the farmers
may get the benefit of bank loans; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

3
Complaints regarding loan waivers
†*8.  SHRI BRIJLAL KHABRI: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has received complaints about banks not
waiving loans without bribe under
‘Agricultural Loan Waiver and Loan Relief
Scheme, 2008’;
(b) if so, the details of these complaints,
State-wise;
(c) the number of such complaints
disposed of by Government;
(d) by when the rest of the complaints
would be disposed of;
(e) the number of banks found guilty;
and
(f) what action has been taken against
them by Government?
Implementation of GST
*9. SHRI RAMDAS AGARW AL: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether he held any meeting
recently with State Finance Ministers to
implement GST (Goods and Services Tax)
with effect from 1 April, 2010;
(b) if so, the details and the outcome
thereof;
(c) whether Chairman of the
Empowered Committee of State Finance
Ministers has expressed the opinion that it
is not feasible to implement GST from
1 April, 2010;
(d) whether there are any constitutional
implications relating to Centre-State
arrangement in the case of GST; and
(e) if so, how Government proposes to
ensure that the legal contours could be
handled more effectively?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Disruptions of flights due to fog
*10. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIA TION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that disruptions
of flight operations during fog have become
an annual feature during the winters, despite
installation of most modern communication
and navigational systems;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
passengers had general complaints against
lack of timely and correct information,
mistreatment and lack of arrangements by
the airlines;
(c) if so, whether Government has
looked into hardships faced by the
passengers;
(d) if so, whether Government has
issued necessary directions to all the airlines
regarding the standards of public facilities
and information systems; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Recommendations of Kirit Parikh
Committee on fuel pricing
*11. SHRI NAND KISHORE YADA V:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Kirit Parikh Committee
on prices of fuel has submitted its report
to his Ministry;
(b) if so, the details of the
recommendations of the Committee;
(c) the details of the prices of different
fuels increased during the last three years,
fuel-wise; and
(d) the action taken by Government to
lower the prices of fuels during the last
three years?

4
H1N1 pandemic status
*12. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) what is the criterion to declare a
disease pandemic or epidemic;
(b) whether H1N1 is pandemic;
(c) the number of  annual casualties due
to Tuberculosis and diarrhoea in India,
separately;
(d) whether attention of Government
has been drawn to the fact that Tamiflu,
the drug for treatment of swine flu, was
aggressively pushed the world over
without adequate medical reasons for its
widespread prescription and the
pharmaceutical companies have become
beneficiaries by sale of drug for swine flu;
and
(e) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto?
Complaints of substandard services by
private airlines
*13. SHRIMA TI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
A VIA TION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has received
complaints of substandard services being
provided by the private airlines in the
country;
(b) if so, the number of such complaints
received during the last two years and the
current year, airline-wise; and
(c) the action Government has taken
against the concerned airlines on such
complaints?
Non-sharing of marketing margin by
RIL
*14. SHRI AMAR SINGH: Will the
Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Reliance
Industries Limited (RIL) is not sharing with
Government the revenue it is collecting from
customers under the marketing margin;
(b) if so, the action initiated by
Government to claim its share of revenue
from the marketing margin from RIL; and
(c) if not, the reasons for not claiming
Government share of marketing margin?
Rural Self-employment Training
Institute Scheme
†*15. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of proposals received
under Rural Self-employment Training
Institute Scheme and how many of them
have been sanctioned, State-wise; and
(b) the percentage of expenditure which
would be met by the Central Government,
Institute-wise?
Special package for Air India
*16. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: Will the
Minister of CIVIL A VIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Central Government has
given any special package for the revival of
financial position of Air India;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether with the introduction of
package, Air India could revive its financial
position?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

5
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Separate fund for empowerment of
Panchayats
*17. SHRI KISHORE KUMAR
MOHANTY: W ill the Minister of
PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state:
(a) the funds provided to the
Panchayats for the development of villages
in Orissa during the last three years;
(b) whether Government proposes to
set up a separate fund for the empowerment
of Panchayats;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the progress achieved in this regard,
so far?
Interest rates on fixed deposits
†*18. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the interest
rates on fixed deposits have been reduced;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the
new interest rates along with new interest
rates fixed for senior citizens; and
(c) whether a hike in interest rates on
fixed deposits for senior citizens is being
considered?
Rising inflation
*19. SHRI D. RAJA: Will the Minister
of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the annual
food inflation based on Wholesale Price
Index (WPI) has risen further to 17.56 per
cent for the week ending 23 January, 2010;
(b) if so, the details of the rise in general
inflation and food inflation between the
weeks ending January, 2009 and January,
2010; and
(c) what are the reasons for such
unabated and unprecedented rise in inflation
rates during the period and Government's
reaction thereto?
Steps taken to tackle spiralling prices
*20. SHRI V . HANUMANTHA RAO:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether he has stated that increasing
foodgrain productivity, ensuring effective
distribution of subsidized essentials to
vulnerable groups and allowing duty free
imports were some of  the steps taken by
Government to control the spiralling prices
of essential commodities;
(b) if so, whether he has also urged
States to ensure effective public
distribution system;
(c) whether wholesale prices based
index of food articles dropped by 1.30 per
cent for week ended 12 December from
19.52 per cent a week ago; and
(d) if so, what are the main steps
Ministry has taken to reduce food prices
further in 2010-11 and to what extent they
have been successful?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 17th February, 2010 Secretary-General.
Magha 28, 1931 (Saka)

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Civil Aviation : 4, 10, 13, 16,
Finance : 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 18, 19, 20,
Health and Family Welfare : 12,
Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises : —
Panchayati Raj : 17,
Petroleum and Natural Gas : 1, 5, 6, 11, 14,
Rural Development : 15.
Shipping : —
6
MGIPMRND—293RS—17.02.2010.
